name: Load Imbalance Factors
text:
# Load Imbalance Factors
## Overview
Load Imbalance Factors are the five primary sources of workload disparity in [parallel volume ray-casting on unstructured grids](#3615-exterior-face-ray-casting.md) [S1, unofficial]. They identify the geometric and data-dependent variables that prevent static [load balancing](#19162-load-balancing.md) from achieving uniform execution times across processors [S1, unofficial].
## How it works
Inputs: empirical timing results from parallel execution on distributed processors. Outputs: a categorized list of the five factors causing workload variance. The method categorizes the sources of variance in processor execution time rather than computing a single scalar metric [S1, unofficial]. It is derived from empirical timing results where the difference between maximum and minimum processing times increased from approximately 40% to 66%, and the proportion of time devoted to ray-casting due to load imbalance reached approximately 33% [S1, unofficial]. The five factors are:
1. **Subvolume size: number of elements**: The count of unstructured grid elements assigned to a processor [S1, unofficial].
2. **Subvolume size: physical size (projected area)**: The physical extent of the subvolume projected onto the image plane [S1, unofficial].
3. **[Opacity transfer functions](#12435-piecewise-function-scalar-opacity-transfer.md)**: The mapping from scalar data values to opacity [S1, unofficial].
4. **Viewing angle**: The orientation of the camera relative to the unstructured grid [S1, unofficial].
5. **Zoom in/out**: The magnification level of the view [S1, unofficial].
## Subtopics

### [Load Imbalance Metric](2763-load-imbalance-metric.md)
Quantifies performance degradation from uneven workload distribution by normalizing the disparity between the slowest and average processors, providing a dimensionless ratio of inefficiency. It is chosen when assessing the global impact of static load balancing failures on total rendering time rather than tracking per-pixel variance.

## Operating characteristics
The factors are qualitative descriptors of workload variance observed through timing analysis of parallel execution [S1, unofficial]. Static partitioning schemes attempt to mitigate imbalance by partitioning a data volume into $n-p$ subvolumes and distributing them in a round-robin fashion among $p$ processors [S1, unofficial]. Increasing $n$ reduces the disparity in average projected areas and element counts per processor, but increases overhead from managing many disjointed subvolumes and ray segments [S1, unofficial]. Consequently, achieving uniform execution times statically remains difficult [S1, unofficial].
## Background
The factors were identified in research on [parallel volume ray-casting](#2592-distributed-parallel-volume-ray-casting-for-unstructured-gri.md) for unstructured-grid data on distributed-memory architectures [S1, unofficial]. The study demonstrated that inherent geometric and data-dependent variables cause significant performance degradation even when static load balancing is applied [S1, unofficial].
## Sources
[S1] DTIC ADA301855: Parallel Volume Ray-Casting for Unstructured-Grid Data on Distributed-Memory Architectures., https://archive.org/details/DTIC_ADA301855, fetched 2026-10-26 (unofficial)
